goal: Arrow-key navigation to replace pure Tab-based keyboard navigation

current_state.navigation_mechanism: Tab key cycles forward through all focusable elements in order. No Shift+Tab or Up/Down support. Home/Settings are mouse-only.
current_state.tab_switching: active-tab property (int: 0=Home, 1=Animations, 2=Borders, 3=Shaders). Each tab is a Rectangle with `width: root.active-tab == N ? 100% : 0%` (triggers Slint layout recomputation). Sidebar NavButtons set active-tab via `clicked => { root.active-tab = nav-module.tab-index; }`.
current_state.focus_management: Each NavButton and PresetCard has a FocusScope with `focus-on-click: false; focus-on-tab-navigation: true;`. Tab navigation works but is forward-only. Enter/Space activate the item. FocusScopes reject unknown keys (propagating to parent).

left_right_arrows.context: Global — works from anywhere in the content area
left_right_arrows.behavior: Left = previous tab, Right = next tab. Cycle through tabs 1-2-3 (Animations, Borders, Shaders). Home (tab 0) and Settings are mouse-only — no arrow access.

up_down_arrows.context: Only within Animations, Borders, or Shaders tabs
up_down_arrows.behavior: Up = move keyboard focus to previous PresetCard in the list, Down = move keyboard focus to next PresetCard. Should NOT navigate through non-card elements (SectionHeader, GeometrySlider, etc.). Should visually indicate which card has keyboard focus (separate from `active`/selected state). Enter/Space toggles the focused card.

tab_shift_tab.behavior: Tab and Shift+Tab should continue to cycle through ALL focusable elements (standard focus order), with Shift+Tab going backward. Up/Down are the fast path for PresetCard-only navigation.

file_layout.ui/main.slint: MainWindow: contains sidebar + content area with 4 tab Rectangles. Owns active-tab property, nav-modules data, and all i18n/callbacks.
file_layout.ui/components.slint: NavButton (sidebar), PresetCard (preset list items), SectionHeader, GeometrySlider, etc.
file_layout.ui/modules.slint: AnimationsModule (line 326), BordersModule (line 359), ShadersModule (line 401). Each has a ScrollView with for-loop rendering PresetCards.
file_layout.src/main.rs: Rust entry point, sets up Slint window and connects callbacks.

NavButton.structure: Rectangle with FocusScope(nb-fs) + TouchArea(nb-ta). Handles Enter/Space to fire clicked(). Rejects other keys. focus-on-tab-navigation: true.
NavButton.navigation_role: Selecting with Left/Right would be nice but not primary — mouse/sidebar is fine.

PresetCard.structure: Rectangle with FocusScope(fs) + TouchArea(ta). active property controls visual state (applied preset). Has acordeón-like expand on active/hover. Handles Enter/Space to fire toggled(). Rejects other keys. focus-on-tab-navigation: true.
PresetCard.navigation_role: Primary target for Up/Down navigation. Needs keyboard-focused visual distinct from active.

AnimationsModule.structure: ScrollView > VerticalLayout > SectionHeader + for-loop of PresetCards. Each card has: title, desc, tag, accent, active, toggled(). No arrow handling at all.
AnimationsModule.navigation_role: Nearest common ancestor for PresetCards — ideal place for focused-index management.

challenges.slint_for_loop_references: In Slint, `for i in model: Element { ... }` does not expose individual iterations as named references that can be used with `forward-focus`. This makes it hard to programmatically jump focus to a specific card based on index.
challenges.focus_movement_api: Slint's FocusScope has no built-in 'focus_next_sibling()' or 'focus_previous_sibling()' method. Tab/Shift+Tab work natively but only through the full document order. There is no Slint-side API to restrict focus movement to items within a specific container.
challenges.focus_vs_selection: Need to distinguish between 'keyboard focus indicator' (which card responds to Enter/Space) and 'active/selected state' (which preset is applied). Currently only active exists.
challenges.key_event_propagation: If PresetCard handles Up/Down, it must accept the event (prevent propagation to parent FocusScopes). But if at the END of the list, Up at index 0 could be propagated to MainWindow for tab switching. Non-trivial event routing.
challenges.scroll_view_integration: Each module is a ScrollView. If Up/Down moves focus to a card outside the visible viewport, the ScrollView should auto-scroll. Slint's ScrollView does NOT auto-scroll to focused elements — requires manual viewport-y calculation.
challenges.slint_focus_on_for_loop_children: Calling .focus() on a FocusScope inside a for loop from the parent is not straightforward — no direct element reference available.

proposed_approaches.name: Minimal — Left/Right via MainWindow FocusScope
proposed_approaches.description: Add a FocusScope at MainWindow level that handles Left/Right arrow keys to change active-tab. Up/Down are not touched — Tab continues to be the only way through presets. Shift+Tab assumed to work natively.
proposed_approaches.limitations: Does not solve the unidirectional Tab problem. User still has to Tab through everything to go back up.

proposed_approaches.name: Focused-index approach
proposed_approaches.description: Each module gets a `focused-index` property. PresetCards get `focus-up` and `focus-down` callbacks. The module handles these to update focused-index. Visual keyboard-focus indicator on the matching card. Actual Slint keyboard focus is handled by mounting a FocusScope PER CARD with conditional forward-focus, or by using a trick with a named FocusScope at the module level whose forward-focus targets change based on focused-index.
proposed_approaches.key_mechanism: Since Slint's for-loop elements can't be referenced directly, use a pattern where each PresetCard checks `keyboard-focused: root.focused-index == i` and changes its visual state. The REAL keyboard focus stays on a container FocusScope, and Enter/Space at the container level is forwarded to the right card based on focused-index. Up/Down change focused-index, which changes the visual indicator + the target of Enter/Space.
proposed_approaches.limitations: The actual keyboard focus (blue ring or default Slint focus indicator) may not match the visual focused-index. Two indicators could be confusing. Also, if user clicks a card with the mouse, the focused-index must sync.
open_questions: Does Slint support `forward-focus` pointing to child items of a `for` loop by index?
Can we call `.focus()` on a for-loop child from Rust via the Slint runtime API?
Does the ScrollView support programmatic scroll-to-element?

proposed_approaches.name: Rust-side keyboard handling
proposed_approaches.description: Handle all keyboard events in Rust (via slint::Window::on_key_pressed or similar). Track focused-index in Rust state. Move Slint focus programmatically via the component tree.
proposed_approaches.pros: Full control, no Slint expression limitations. Can sync focus and visual state easily.
proposed_approaches.cons: More boilerplate. Need to expose Slint internal element references to Rust (possible via `global().get_ property` and `slint::ComponentHandle`).
open_questions: Can Rust iterate over for-loop generated elements and call focus() on them?
What's the best way to get a reference to a specific FocusScope inside a repeated component?

specific_questions_for_consultation: 1. In Slint, what is the idiomatic way to move keyboard focus between items in a `for` loop using Arrow keys (Up/Down)?
2. Can a named element inside a `for` loop (e.g., `for i in model: card := PresetCard { ... }`) be referenced by index (e.g., `card[index]`) for `forward-focus` purposes?
3. Does Slint's FocusScope support calling `.focus()` from Rust on a specific element inside a repeated component? If so, what's the API?
4. Does Slint's ScrollView provide any automatic scroll-to-focused-element behavior, or must viewport-y be manually set on focus change?
5. How can a FocusScope handle Up/Down to move focus to the previous/next sibling FocusScope within the same parent? Is there a built-in focus-traversal API beyond Tab/Shift+Tab?
6. Is there a way to restrict Tab/Shift+Tab focus order to a subset of elements (e.g., only PresetCards within a module, skipping SectionHeader)?

success_criteria.left_right: Arrow keys switch between tabs 1-2-3 without layout glitches or focus loss.
success_criteria.up_down: Up/Down keys move a visible keyboard-focus indicator between PresetCards within the active tab. Cards outside viewport cause auto-scroll.
success_criteria.focus_indicator: Keyboard-focused card has a clear visual distinction from the active/selected card (e.g., a bright focus ring or different background).
success_criteria.tab_shift_tab: Continue to work for full-document focus traversal, backward and forward.
success_criteria.click_sync: Clicking a card with the mouse moves keyboard focus there as well.
success_criteria.no_regression: Existing mouse and Tab navigation continues to work unchanged.
